thread.title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Squanders Early Gain as Apple, Conflicting Trade Reports Weigh

title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Squanders Early Gain as Apple, Conflicting Trade Reports Weigh

organizations.name: utilities moving the market u.s. president trump

text:
Strong: Energy, Consumer Discretionary, Financials, Industrials Weak: Information Technology, Real Estate, Consumer Staples, Utilities Moving the Market
U.S. President Trump reportedly has asked his cabinet to draft a trade deal between the U.S. and China; senior White House official clarifies there is still a long way to go
Apple (AAPL) weighs on the broader market
Exxon Mobile (XOM), Chevron (CVX) help pare Dow losses with positive earnings reports
October nonfarm payrolls increased by 250,000 (Briefing.com consensus +190,000); Unemployment rate unchanged at 3.7% S&P 500 Squanders Early Gain as Apple, Conflicting Trade Reports Weigh 02-Nov-18 13:05 ET Dow -257.80 at 25122.94, Nasdaq -128.68 at 7305.57, S&P -36.31 at 2704.20
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has squandered an early gain after a conflicting report surrounding China trade developments tempered previous trade optimism. The benchmark index has taken a dive into negative territory, trading lower by 1.0%. In addition, Apple 's (AAPL 2017.16, -15.12, -6.8%) disappointing outlook has weighed on the heavily-weighted information technology sector (-1.9%) and the broader market.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite is down 1.4%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 0.8%, and the Russell 2000 is down 0.3%.
A Bloomberg report last night indicated that U.S. President Trump had asked his cabinet to draft a trade deal between the U.S. and China. However, a CNBC report dampened sentiment after it said White House sources indicated that there was no truth to the prior report. Larry Kudlow on CNBC chimed in, saying the cabinet was not asked by President Trump to draw up a trade plan for China -- officially denying the Bloomberg report from sources.
Separately, Apple disappointed investors by guiding its fiscal Q1 revenue slightly below Wall Street's expectations. The company stated that it is seeing some emerging markets pressure in India, Brazil, Russia, and Turkey, but Chinese demand remains strong. Additionally, Apple will no longer provide unit-sales data for the iPhone, iPad, and Mac beginning this quarter.
In other earnings, energy Dow components Exxon Mobil (XOM 80.40, -0.28, -0.4%) and Chevron (CVX 113.67, +2.52, +2.3%) are mixed despite both companies beating earnings expectations. The S&P 500 energy sector is down 1.0%. On a related note, WTI crude is down 1.1% to $63.01/bbl.
Also in focus today was the consequential Employment Situation report for October, which showed a nonfarm payrolls increase of 250,000, higher than the Briefing.com consensus of 190,000. Also, as expected, average hourly earnings increased 0.2% and the unemployment rate remained at 3.7%. In short, the strong jobs report corroborated labor market trends that will keep the Federal Reserve on a tightening path.
Subsequently, demand for U.S. Treasuries has decreased, pushing yields higher across the curve. The Fed-sensitive 2-yr yield is currently up four basis points to 2.88%, and the benchmark 10-yr yield is up five basis points to 3.19%. Also, of note, the U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.3% to 96.53.
Overseas, Asian markets rallied on last night's trade report with Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+4.2%) leading the advance and China's Shanghai Composite climbing 2.7%. In Europe, the Euro Stoxx 50 added 0.3%.
Reviewing today's economic data, which included the Employment Situation report for October, the Trade Balance report for September, and the Factory Orders report for September: October nonfarm payrolls increased by 250,000 while the Briefing.com consensus expected an increase of 190,000. The prior month's increase was revised to 118,000 from 134,000. Nonfarm private payrolls rose by 246,000 while the Briefing.com consensus expected an increase of 185,000. The previous month's increase was unrevised at 121,000. Average hourly earnings increased 0.2% (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%), while the previous month's increase was unrevised at 0.3%. The average workweek was reported at 34.5 (Briefing.com consensus 34.5). The unemployment rate remained at 3.7% in October (Briefing.com consensus 3.7%). The key takeaway from the October employment report is that it is consistent with labor market trends that will keep the Federal Reserve on a tightening path The Trade Balance Report for September showed a widening in the trade deficit to $54.0 billion (Briefing.com consensus -$53.4B) from a downwardly revised $53.3 billion (from -$53.2 billion) in August. The key takeaway from the report is the same as last month in that it has yet to confirm the tariff actions are succeeding in cutting the trade deficit with China specifically and in general. Factory orders increased 0.7% in September (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) following an upwardly revised 2.6% increase (from +2.3%) in August. Excluding transportation, orders were up 0.4% for the second straight month. The key takeaway from the report was the understanding that shipments of nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft -- the component that factors into GDP forecasts -- declined for the second straight month.
